newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tankers mainly unchanged, VLCCs seen dipping.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tankers mainly unchanged, VLCCs seen dipping.

text.p: Dirty tanker rates ended an uneventful week little changed, with very large and ultra large crude carriers (VLCCs) soft and likely to remain so next week, brokers said.

Galbraith's Ltd said in their weekly tanker report: "There is definite pressure being brought to bear upon owners who are having to accept below 'last done' in order to persuade charterers to book their vessels.
"Even on ULCCs (ultra-large crude carriers) that, until now, have held their own, a similar scenario is appearing."
"Next week could actually be busier as many charterers, particularly those in the Far East, get confirmation on their stem nominations for first half of May.
"However, it is unlikely that rates will be improved by this; availability for this period is quite fluid and even includes four or five Japanese oil company relets," Galbraith's added.

Although Mideast VLCC rates are down on last week, especially to Japan and South Korea which are about four Worldscale points lower, owners may be able to gain some comfort from the fact that they are well above year ago levels.
Galbraith's figures show Mideast/Japan VLCC rates currently at W61.13 against W54.75 a year ago and Mideast/U.K.-Cont now at W54 compared with W47.50.
Transatlantic VLCCs were steady at around W65/70, with 130,000 tonners (Suezmaxes) at W95.
The latter market was generally more resilient than VLCCs, with West Africa/U.S. Gulf trips steady at W97.5, while the Mediterranean market was active with cargoes fixed around W85.

The Med 80,000 tonne (Aframax) sector edged up to around W120 on Friday after drifting as low as W110 as enquiry increased modestly, an Italian broker said. Inter-U.K./Cont Aframaxes were unchanged at W100.
The Caribs/upcoast crude market remained strong with 70,000 tonnes at W220/W230, but 50,000 tonnes of fuel oil dipped to W195 from W205 on a lack of enquiry, brokers said.
The European fuel oil market was dormant, with inter-U.K./Cont 25,000 tonne cargoes dipping to W180 or slightly lower and cross-Med unchanged at W200.
